title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes, M is almost certainly the Q-linear Tannakian category of motives over a finite field F_q (q a power of p). Two clues point that way. First, the last line mentions H^2(Q_p, ...). Second, motives over a number field have a Betti fibre functor over Q, so the statement 'no fibre functor over R' would be false for them. G is the motivic Galois group (more precisely a gerbe or groupoid, because no Q-valued fibre functor exists), and G° is its identity component. xi is the class in a nonabelian/abelian H^2(Q, band) of the gerbe of fibre functors. It is the obstruction to finding a fibre functor over Q. xi_v denotes its image in H^2(Q_v, band) for v = l finite or v = infinity.

First paragraph (end of an argument begun on the previous manuscript page). The 'infinite' contributions and certain components vanish. By a Hasse-principle and reciprocity argument, the analogue for the band of 0 -> Br Q -> (+)_v Br Q_v -> Q/Z -> 0, one gets: xi is known once all xi_l (l finite) are known. So xi is determined by its finite local components.

NB paragraph. It is known that M has no fibre functor over R, hence none over Q. Three reasons are offered:
(1) A structural reason, read tentatively as 'M is p-divisible/discontinuous'; the reading is uncertain.
(2) A real fibre functor would yield a degree-1, rank-1 representation (an invertible object of odd weight) of G°. The obstruction to this lies in an Ext^2(Z, ...) (crossed out) and does not come from G; such a rank-1, degree-1 theory would itself give a fibre functor.
(3) The classical argument with elliptic curves: a supersingular elliptic curve has endomorphism algebra the quaternion algebra over Q ramified exactly at p and infinity. This algebra cannot act on a 2-dimensional R-vector space, nor on a 2-dimensional Q_p-vector space. This is Serre's argument, linked here to Hasse–Weil.

Consequence. A fortiori xi_infty != 0. The component of xi_infty along H^2(R, K_R), with K the (pro-)torus at the centre of the band (the Weil-number torus), is the image of something nonzero. Via the reciprocity/duality relation it depends on the remaining local component. Since the l-adic realisations (l != p) give fibre functors over Q_l, xi_l = 0 for l != p. Hence that remaining component is xi_p, lying in H^2(Q_p, ...), which is the crystalline obstruction.

In short, the page sets up the local-global description of the class of the motivic gerbe over F_q: trivial at l != p, nontrivial at p and at infinity, the two linked by reciprocity.
errors: The claim that xi is determined by its finite local components needs care. It requires Sha^2(Q, band) = 0 and a Tate–Nakayama type reciprocity for the (pro-)torus K. For a general torus Sha^2 can be nonzero, and for a pro-torus there are lim^1 issues (cf. Milne's treatment). The page asserts this without justification, as far as can be read.
The precise first reason ('M p-divisible / discontinu') is too illegible to check.
The rank-1, degree-1 argument is only sketched: the Ext^2 obstruction is crossed out and left unexplained.

ideas.what: Class xi of the gerbe of fibre functors of the Tannakian category of motives over F_q, studied through its local components xi_l, xi_p, xi_infty
ideas.modern_name: Motivic gerbe over a finite field / Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid; local description of its cohomology class
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport (1987); Milne, 'Motives over finite fields' (1994); framework in Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own published texts as far as I know. Tannakian gerbes were developed in Saavedra's thesis following Grothendieck's ideas.

ideas.what: No fibre functor over R (or Q, Q_p) for motives over F_p, via the supersingular elliptic curve whose endomorphism algebra is the quaternion algebra ramified at p and infinity
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck–Serre correspondence (1964) discusses motives; Saavedra Ch. VI

ideas.what: xi_l = 0 for l != p, so xi is determined by xi_p and xi_infty, which are linked by reciprocity, and xi_infty != 0
ideas.modern_name: Local triviality away from p, infinity of the motivic gerbe; Hasse principle for its class

ideas.what: Obstruction to a rank-1, odd-weight ('degree 1, rank 1') object, expressed as an Ext^2 class not coming from G
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to a 'half Tate twist' / splitting of the weight cocharacter over R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed by Deligne, Milne (Weil-number torus, weight cocharacter); Serre's 'motivic Galois group' remarks

missed.claim: Already in 1965, Grothendieck treats the class of the gerbe of fibre functors on motives over a finite field as an H^2 class over Q. He decomposes it into local components, uses l-adic realisations to kill xi_l (l != p), and deduces xi_infty != 0 from the nonexistence of real fibre functors, linking it to the component in H^2(Q_p, ...). This is the strategy later carried out by Langlands–Rapoport and Milne for the pseudomotivic groupoid.
missed.quote: Donc on connaît ξ quand on connaît tous les ξ_ℓ (ℓ fini) ... A fortiori, ξ_∞ ≠ 0 ... la composante de ξ_∞ suivant H^2(R, K_R) ... dans H^2(Q_p, ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the local-global description of the motivic gerbe over F_q, central to Langlands–Rapoport and to Milne's work on Shimura-variety point counting, was envisaged by Grothendieck two decades earlier. That matters for attribution and for the history of motivic Galois groups.

missed.claim: There is a sketched alternative proof of nonexistence of real fibre functors via a rank-1, degree-1 representation of G° whose Ext^2 obstruction does not come from G. This is an intrinsic, weight-theoretic argument rather than one depending on supersingular curves.
missed.quote: on aurait une représentation de G° de degré 1, rang 1 (qui ne provient pas de G) ... l'obstruction étant dans Ext^2(Z, ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a cleaner, group-theoretic obstruction in terms of the central torus and the weight cocharacter. It could be compared with Milne's and Deligne's treatment of the Weil-number torus.

deep.surprise_reason: The objects are now standard, but seeing Grothendieck in 1965 analyse local components xi_l, xi_p, xi_infty of the motivic gerbe class over F_q is an early, little-known anticipation of Langlands–Rapoport/Milne. The page is fragmentary, so it is not a decisive new result.
transcription_corrections: The third reason probably reads 'soit par l'argument de Serre ... sur les courbes elliptiques (supersingulières)'; 'formes [?]' is likely 'Serre'.
The first paragraph likely ends 'Donc on ... connaît ξ' (i.e. ξ is known/determined).
The final line 'dans H^2(Q_p, H_2)' is likely H^2(Q_p, K_p) or similar, matching H^2(R, K_R).
